dispositions.summary: All required frames show three-vane canoe form; offset quilt/module relief is present; frontal view conveys the central vane and upcurved laterals, top shows trough/seam. Small matrix is visible as a narrow underside support; there is no bead ornament or fully living-organism reconstruction. Based on actual UT/Paleobiology Fig.1/3 pixels and frozen specimen-study scope. 491 reported noncoplanar contacts are between the fossil and its intended matrix support; no blanket zero-intersection gate was applied; coplanar positive-area check has zero hits and reviewed frames show no visible z-fighting.

A broad domed mound is continuous with a flat tundra base, summit fissures are irregular rather than a circular crater, and one side sector exposes the pale-blue schematic core beneath a narrow soil edge. Reference and frozen brief explicitly avoid asserting this is an actual Ibyuk core or exact named-site reconstruction. Cutaway is prominent but limited to one bounded sector and does not imply broad natural ice exposure.

Dark tabular body follows inclined host beds and projects as a resistant ledge; pale narrow contact bands appear above and below it; several subdued host layers and shallow blocky joints are visible. It reads as an intrusive sill rather than a vertical dike, coal seam, or lava flow. Assessment stays generic and does not claim an exact Purcell/Sexton locality clone.

One coherent rounded granite mass retains a mostly continuous crown, with two broad irregular local shell patches that follow shoulders and show restrained physical undercut gaps. No regular horizontal tiers/scales or literal Half Dome split event is implied; generic simplified Sentinel Dome teaching scope preserved.
